requirements: Reproduce Gated DeltaNet-2, a linear-attention layer that decouples erase and write via channel-wise gates, including its chunkwise training algorithm, hybrid architecture, and empirical results at 1.3B parameters on 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens across language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and retrieval benchmarks.

sub_tasks.requirements: Establish the hardware, software, and training infrastructure required to train and evaluate Gated DeltaNet-2 and baselines at 1.3B scale.
Provide the hardware and GPU-level infrastructure needed for training and throughput measurement.
Code has been implemented to run training and throughput benchmarks on NVIDIA H100 GPUs (as used in Section 4 and Figure 2), including detection/verification of the GPU architecture at runtime.

The training infrastructure supports both Hopper (H100) and Ampere GPUs, with Hopper-specific handling of the fused WY backward kernel that restricts the Triton warp autotuning search to {2, 4} warps to avoid the WGMMA layout assertion for the 64x64 accumulator, while the full search space is retained on Ampere.
Set up the software stack (PyTorch, Triton, distributed training) required to compile and run the Gated DeltaNet-2 kernels and training loop.
Code has been implemented to install and configure Triton for compiling the fused forward, backward, and recurrent decoding kernels of Gated Delta Rule-2 (referenced in Section 3.3 and Section C).
Code has been implemented to set up a PyTorch training environment with mixed-precision support (bfloat16 activations with fp32 accumulators / fp32 state) as described in Section D.3.

Code has been implemented to enable multi-GPU distributed data-parallel training capable of sustaining the global batch size of 0.5M tokens at sequence length 4K required for 1.3B-parameter pretraining on 100B tokens.
Provide numerical precision infrastructure for the recurrent kernels and state, consistent with Section D.

The log-decay tensor g_t is computed in explicit fp32 outside the kernel before being consumed by the chunk kernels, so that cumulative log-decay sums do not incur bfloat16/fp16 mantissa precision loss (Section C.1, Section D.1).

The recurrent state S is stored in fp32 across chunks and during recurrent decoding, and all matrix-multiplication accumulators inside the chunk kernels use fp32 accumulation, with the layer output cast back to the model dtype at the kernel boundary (Section D.3).

An explicit precision flag is exposed for the triangular solve A = (I + T)^{-1}, allowing a conservative IEEE fp32 path when required while permitting the faster tensor-core path for the remaining matrix products (Section D.4).
Provide data-loading and sequence-packing infrastructure for training at the specified sequence length and batch size.

Code has been implemented to provide a data-loading pipeline that streams FineWeb-Edu tokens and produces batches of training sequence length 4K tokens with a global batch size of 0.5M tokens (i.e., ~128 sequences per global batch).

Code has been implemented to support packed variable-length batches via cumulative sequence lengths (cu_seqlens), with the chunk index construction resetting the recurrent state at every sequence boundary, and the same layout consumed by the chunk forward, chunk backward, and recurrent decoding kernels (Section C.6).
Provide training-loop infrastructure (optimizer, scheduler, checkpointing) shared across all recurrent and hybrid model runs.

Code has been implemented to instantiate an AdamW optimizer wrapper with gradient clipping at 1.0 and cosine learning-rate decay with a 1B-token linear warm-up, driven by processed token count, so it can be reused identically for all model families.

Code has been implemented to periodically checkpoint model weights, optimizer state, LR-scheduler state, and token counter, and to resume training deterministically from a checkpoint, enabling completion of 100B-token runs across interruptions.

Code has been implemented to log training loss, learning rate, throughput (tokens/sec), and gradient norm at a regular interval throughout the 100B-token training run, so that Figure 2-style throughput measurements and run health can be inspected.
Provide throughput-benchmarking infrastructure used to reproduce Figure 2.

Code has been implemented to run a single-H100 training-step throughput benchmark that iterates over the (sequence length, batch size) configurations 2K x 8, 4K x 4, 8K x 2, and 16K x 1 (matching Figure 2), warms up the CUDA graph/allocator, and reports thousands of tokens per second (Kt/s) for each configuration.

The throughput benchmark harness invokes exactly the same model implementations (Transformer, Mamba-2, Mamba-3 SISO, Mamba-3 MIMO, Gated DeltaNet, KDA, Gated DeltaNet-2) as used in training, in their hybrid 1.3B configurations, so that the Figure 2 comparison is apples-to-apples.

Prepare FineWeb-Edu pretraining data and all evaluation datasets (WikiText, LAMBADA, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e/c, OpenBookQA, SIQA, BoolQ, RULER S-NIAH/MK-NIAH, SWDE, FDA, SQuAD, TriviaQA, DROP, NQ).
Acquire and prepare the FineWeb-Edu pretraining corpus for 100B-token training runs.
Code has been implemented to download or stream the FineWeb-Edu dataset (Penedo et al., 2024) from its public source (e.g. HuggingFace hub) into a local or shard-addressable store.

Code has been implemented to tokenize FineWeb-Edu documents with the model tokenizer and pack them into contiguous 4K-token training sequences with document boundaries handled consistently (e.g. via EOS separators or packed variable-length layout).
The prepared FineWeb-Edu training set provides at least 100B tokens sampled/packed for consumption, matching the training budget stated in Section 4/E.1.
Code has been implemented for a deterministic (seeded) data loader that yields packed 4K-token batches producing the specified 0.5M-token global batch size for training.
Prepare language-modeling perplexity evaluation datasets (WikiText and LAMBADA).

Code has been implemented to load the WikiText test split used for perplexity evaluation and to tokenize/segment it using the same tokenizer as the pretrained models for word-level perplexity reporting consistent with Table 2.

Code has been implemented to load the LAMBADA evaluation set and to prepare it both for perplexity computation (ppl) and for zero-shot last-word accuracy (acc), matching the two LAMBADA columns in Table 2.
Prepare zero-shot commonsense and reading-comprehension evaluation datasets used in Table 2.

Code has been implemented to load PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, OpenBookQA, SIQA, and BoolQ evaluation splits through a standardized harness (e.g. lm-evaluation-harness) with the zero-shot task configurations matching the suite used by prior recurrent LM work (Gu & Dao, 2023).

The evaluation configuration reports HellaSwag using length-normalized accuracy (acc_n) while all other commonsense tasks (PIQA, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA, SIQA, BoolQ) use plain accuracy (acc), matching the metric annotations in Table 2.
Prepare RULER synthetic needle-in-a-haystack retrieval datasets for Table 3.

Code has been implemented to construct the RULER S-NIAH-1 (passkey), S-NIAH-2 (numerical needle), and S-NIAH-3 (word needle) tasks following Hsieh et al. (2024), producing evaluation examples at context lengths 1K, 2K, 4K, and 8K as reported in Table 3.
Code has been implemented to construct the RULER MK-NIAH-1 multi-key task with distractor key-value pairs at context lengths 1K, 2K, and 4K, matching the MK-NIAH-1 columns in Table 3.

The RULER data generation uses a fixed random seed and produces a deterministic set of needle/haystack samples per (task, context length) pair so that reported accuracies are reproducible across runs.
Prepare real-world in-context retrieval datasets (SWDE, FDA, SQuAD, TriviaQA, NQ, DROP) for Table 4.

Code has been implemented to load SWDE (structured HTML relation extraction) and FDA (key-value retrieval from PDFs) following the Just-Read-Twice recall suite (Arora et al., 2024) as used in Table 4.
Code has been implemented to load the SQuAD, TriviaQA, Natural Questions, and DROP question-answering datasets in the retrieval-style formatting used by the Table 4 evaluation suite.
Code has been implemented to truncate real-world retrieval inputs to a 2K-token context window prior to model evaluation, matching the '2K truncation' setting used in Table 4.

Code has been implemented to score each real-world retrieval task with its appropriate accuracy/EM-style metric (per Just-Read-Twice conventions) and to output per-task accuracies together with the six-task macro-average used in Table 4.
Provide a unified tokenizer and data-format layer shared by pretraining and all evaluation datasets.

The pretraining and evaluation code use the same tokenizer/vocabulary for all 1.3B models, so that WikiText/LAMBADA perplexities and zero-shot log-likelihood comparisons across baselines are computed under identical tokenization.

Code has been implemented to expose all prepared evaluation datasets through a common interface (e.g. task registry keyed by task name) that emits (input_ids, target, metric) triples consumable by the evaluation runner, so downstream Table 2/3/4 scripts can iterate them uniformly.
Implement the core Gated Delta Rule-2 recurrence with channel-wise decay, channel-wise erase gate b_t, and channel-wise write gate w_t, along with correct gate parameterizations.
The tokenwise recurrent update implements Gated Delta Rule-2 correctly, including the erase factor construction, write vector construction, decay application, and output projection.
Code has been implemented that constructs the erase vector e_t = b_t ⊙ k_t as an elementwise product of the channel-wise erase gate b_t ∈ R^{d_k} and the key vector k_t ∈ R^{d_k}.
Code has been implemented that constructs the write vector z_t = w_t ⊙ v_t as an elementwise product of the channel-wise write gate w_t ∈ R^{d_v} and the value vector v_t ∈ R^{d_v}.
Code has been implemented that forms the decayed state ̄S_t = D_t S_{t-1} where D_t = Diag(α_t) applies channel-wise decay along the key dimension prior to the active edit.
Code has been implemented that applies the full Gated Delta Rule-2 state update S_t = (I − k_t e_t^⊤) D_t S_{t-1} + k_t z_t^⊤, matching Equation 9/10 of the paper.
Code has been implemented that computes the output o_t = S_t^⊤ q_t using the state orientation specified in the paper (queries contract along the key axis).
The tokenwise recurrent kernel keeps the state in fp32 and multiplies by exp(g_t) (channel-wise decay) each step, consistent with the recurrent decoding kernel described in Appendix C.5.
The layer produces the erase gate, write gate, and log-decay via the parameterizations specified in Equations 11-12 with correct shapes, ranges, and precision handling.

Code has been implemented that produces the channel-wise erase gate as b_t = sigmoid(W_b x_t) with an independent linear projection of shape d_model → H · d_k, producing values in [0,1]^{d_k} per head.

Code has been implemented that produces the channel-wise write gate as w_t = sigmoid(W_w x_t) with an independent linear projection of shape d_model → H_v · d_v, producing values in [0,1]^{d_v} per value head.

Code has been implemented that computes the log-decay tensor g_t following the Gated DeltaNet parameterization (Equation 12), with a per-head scalar a broadcast across d_k channels and a per-channel bias δ.
The log-decay g_t is computed in explicit fp32 before being consumed by the kernel to avoid precision loss in the cumulative log-decay G_r = Σ_{i≤r} g_i.
The layer computes α_t = exp(g_t) elementwise so that α_t ∈ (0,1]^{d_k} (assuming g_t ≤ 0), yielding a channel-wise decay vector consumable by the recurrence.

Code has been implemented that optionally supports the negative-eigenvalue variant by scaling only the erase gate to the range [0,2]^{d_k} (via multiplying the sigmoid output by 2), while leaving the write gate in [0,1]^{d_v}.
The state update behaves correctly in special cases, recovering KDA and Gated DeltaNet under the appropriate gate tyings and admitting the fast-weight local objective interpretation.

When b_t = β_t · 1_{d_k} and w_t = β_t · 1_{d_v} (both tied to the same scalar per token), the Gated Delta Rule-2 recurrence numerically reproduces the KDA update S_t = (I − β_t k_t k_t^⊤) D_t S_{t-1} + β_t k_t v_t^⊤.
When additionally α_t = α_t · 1_{d_k} (scalar decay), the recurrence reduces numerically to the Gated DeltaNet update S_t = α_t (I − β_t k_t k_t^⊤) S_{t-1} + β_t k_t v_t^⊤.

The update satisfies the fast-weight local objective in Equation 13: given the decayed state ̄S_t = D_t S_{t-1}, the resulting S_t minimizes ||S − ̄S_t||_F^2 − 2⟨S^⊤ k_t, z_t − ̄S_t^⊤ e_t⟩, verifiable by comparing S_t against the closed-form minimizer.
Implement the chunkwise WY-form forward algorithm with decay-normalized state, asymmetric erase factors, and Triton kernels for efficient parallel training.
Set up chunk-level tensor structures and cumulative-decay preprocessing needed by the forward algorithm.

Code has been implemented that splits input sequences into fixed-size chunks of length C=64 for the chunkwise forward pass, with per-chunk tensors Q, K, V, B, W, and log-decay g arranged so that each chunk carries at most C tokens (padding or variable-length packing handled outside the kernel).

Code has been implemented that computes the log-decay tensor g_t in explicit fp32 from the log-decay projection (Eq. 12 / Eq. 86) before it is passed to the kernel, avoiding precision loss in cumulative sums.

Code has been implemented that forms local cumulative log-decay G_r = sum_{i<=r} g_i inside the chunk and produces the elementwise cumulative decay vector gamma_r = exp(G_r), broadcast across the appropriate key channel axis.

Given a small hand-crafted input with known per-token log-decay values, the implementation returns gamma_r values matching exp of the running sum to within fp32 numerical tolerance for every row of the chunk.
Implement the decay-normalized recurrence that absorbs channel-wise decay into asymmetric erase factors.

Code has been implemented that defines the normalized keys k_bar_r = k_r / gamma_r, the asymmetric erase factor e_bar_r = gamma_r ⊙ (b_r ⊙ k_r), and the write vector z_r = w_r ⊙ v_r as specified in Eq. 30 and Eq. 33.
The implementation follows the decay-normalized recurrence S_hat_r = S_hat_{r-1} - k_bar_r e_bar_r^T S_hat_{r-1} + k_bar_r z_r^T (Eq. 32) rather than applying decay to the state at every step.

Code has been implemented that stacks per-row vectors k_bar_r^T, e_bar_r^T, z_r^T into row-major matrices K_bar, E_bar, Z of shape (C, d_k), (C, d_k), (C, d_v) respectively as row inputs to the WY solve.
Implement the WY-form triangular solve producing shared auxiliaries Y and U.
Code has been implemented that constructs the strictly lower triangular matrix T with T_{rs} = e_bar_r^T k_bar_s for s<r and zero otherwise (Eq. 21 / Eq. 34).
Code has been implemented that computes A = (I + T)^{-1} by forward substitution inside each chunk, exploiting that A is lower triangular with unit diagonal.
Code has been implemented that forms the erase-side auxiliary Y = A E_bar and the write-side auxiliary U = A Z, sharing the same inverse A for both right-hand sides (Eq. 22 / Eq. 79).
The WY solve exposes an explicit precision flag so that the triangular solve for A can be performed in IEEE fp32 while remaining matrix products can use faster tensor-core paths.
Implement the end-of-chunk state update and per-token output equation using Y, U, and the tail-key matrix.
Code has been implemented that constructs K_tail whose row r equals (gamma_C / gamma_r) ⊙ k_r, as required by the end-of-chunk state formula.

Code has been implemented that computes the end-of-chunk state S^{[n+1]} = Diag(gamma_C) S_0 + K_tail^T (U - Y S_0) following Eq. 23 / Eq. 40, and carries this state as the initial state of the next chunk.
Code has been implemented that constructs Q_gamma whose row r equals gamma_r ⊙ q_r and the causal score matrix A_qk = tril(Q_gamma K_bar^T) (Eq. 24 / Eq. 43).
Code has been implemented that produces the chunk output block O = Q_gamma S_0 + A_qk (U - Y S_0) following Eq. 24 / Eq. 44.
Implement the fused Triton kernels that realize the chunkwise forward pass on GPU.
A Triton kernel has been implemented that computes the intra-chunk products, forming A_qk and the strictly lower T from decay-normalized keys and the erase-gated key factor (b_r ⊙ k_r ⊙ gamma_r).
A Triton kernel has been implemented that performs the WY forward-substitution solve to build A = (I+T)^{-1} and exposes it to both erase-side and write-side right-hand sides.

A Triton kernel has been implemented that constructs the auxiliaries Y = A E_bar and U = A Z (storing Y under a buffer name compatible with the KDA-style layout while retaining its mathematical role).
A Triton kernel has been implemented that applies the inter-chunk state recurrence (Eq. 40) using K_tail, Y, U, and the incoming state, propagating S across chunks.
A Triton kernel has been implemented that produces the chunk output O from Q_gamma, A_qk, and R = U - Y S_0 (Eq. 44).
The forward kernels keep the recurrent state in fp32 across chunks and use fp32 matrix multiplication accumulators, casting the layer output back to the model dtype only at the kernel boundary.

Autotuning for the fused kernels supports the full Ampere warp search space and restricts the Hopper backward WY kernel warp search to two and four warps to avoid the Triton WGMMA 64x64 layout assertion.
Support variable-length packed batches and a recurrent decoding fallback consistent with the chunkwise algorithm.

Code has been implemented that represents packed variable-length batches with cumulative sequence lengths and resets the recurrent state at every sequence boundary within the chunk forward, chunk backward, and recurrent decoding kernels.

A forward-only recurrent decoding kernel has been implemented that applies Eq. 29 token by token, keeps the state in fp32, multiplies by exp(g_t), reads along b_t ⊙ k_t, writes w_t ⊙ v_t along k_t, and returns S^T q_t.
Establish behavioral correctness of the chunkwise forward against tokenwise reference implementations.
For a random tokenwise reference input, the chunkwise forward output O matches the tokenwise recurrent reference (applying Eq. 29 explicitly) within machine precision when both are computed in fp64.
The end-of-chunk state S^{[n+1]} produced by the chunk kernel matches the tokenwise reference state after C steps for varied C, d_k, d_v, batch, and head configurations.

When b_r = beta_r 1_{d_k} and w_r = beta_r 1_{d_v}, the chunkwise forward numerically reduces to the KDA update, and when additionally alpha_r = alpha_r 1_{d_k}, it reduces to the Gated DeltaNet update, as required by the tied-gate reductions in Appendix A.5.
Implement the gate-aware backward pass with correct vector-Jacobian products through the WY inverse, gates, cumulative decay, and state paths.
Output path backward: propagate gradients from the chunk output block dO through the equation O = A_qk · V_out + Q_gamma · R.
Code has been implemented for a backward kernel that receives the upstream chunk-output gradient dO with matching shape (batch, heads, chunk_size C=64, d_v).

Code has been implemented so that the output-path backward computes dA_qk = tril(dO · R^T) (with the causal mask applied) and dR contribution = A_qk^T · dO, matching Equation 53 and Equation 54 in Appendix B.1.
Code has been implemented to also produce dQ_gamma = dO · R^T contributions that are later routed into dQ and d(gamma), so the Q_gamma factor in Eq. 44 is correctly differentiated.
Inter-chunk state backward: propagate the upstream end-of-chunk state gradient dS_C through the recurrence S_C = Diag(gamma_C) · (S_0 + K_tail^T · R).

Code has been implemented for a state-path backward kernel that consumes dS_C and produces dS_0, d(K_tail), and the state-path contribution to dR, using K_tail, Y, and U as already-computed tensors (structure-equivalent to the KDA state VJP).

Code has been implemented so that the state-path VJP correctly applies the diagonal factor gamma_C (i.e. left-multiplies gradients by Diag(gamma_C)) and emits the corresponding contribution to d(gamma_C) that is later folded into d(gamma).

Code has been implemented so that the residual relation R = U − Y·S_0 is used to split gradients: dU += dR and dY += −dR · S_0^T (equivalently d(YS_0) = −dR), with dS_0 accumulating −Y^T · dR (Equations 55–56).
Gate-aware WY inverse backward: accumulate dA with gate factors baked into the dot products, following Equations 25–26 and Appendix B.2.

Code has been implemented for a dedicated backward kernel that receives dY and dU and produces dA, dE_bar, dZ using the identities dA = dU · Z^T − dY · (E_bar · S_0)^T-style contributions with gates present at the accumulation sites.

The write-side contribution to dA is computed as dA += dU · (W ⊙ V)^T with the write gate W multiplied into V before the outer product, i.e., no scalar post-scaling shortcut is used (implements Equation 25 write term).

The erase-side contribution to dA is computed as dA += dY · (gamma ⊙ B ⊙ K)^T with the erase gate B and cumulative decay gamma multiplied into K before the outer product (implements Equation 26 / erase term of Equation 25).
Code has been implemented for the WY-inverse VJP dT = −A^T · dA · A^T with only the strictly lower triangular part of dT retained (Equation 66–67).

A unit test verifies that replacing the gate-aware accumulation with a KDA-style scalar post-scale of dA produces incorrect gradients when b_t and w_t differ across channels, confirming that the gates must live inside the dot products (Appendix B.5).
Score matrix and tail-key backward: differentiate A_qk = tril(Q_gamma · K_bar^T) and K_tail rows to obtain gradients into Q_gamma and K_bar.
Code has been implemented so that dQ_gamma += tril(dA_qk) · K_bar and dK_bar += tril(dA_qk)^T · Q_gamma, with the causal mask on dA_qk (Equation 68).
Code has been implemented so that the tail-key gradient contribution uses (K_tail)_r = gamma_C ⊙ k_bar_r to route d(K_tail) into dK_bar and into d(gamma_C) (Equation 69).
Elementwise gate and cumulative decay backward: emit dB, dW, and dg from the elementwise relations Z = W ⊙ V and E_bar = gamma ⊙ (B ⊙ K).
Code has been implemented so the backward emits dW = dZ ⊙ V and dV += dZ ⊙ W with the correct write-gate output shape (B, T, H_v, d_v) (Equation 70 / Appendix C.3).
Code has been implemented so the backward emits dB = dE_bar ⊙ gamma ⊙ K and dK += dE_bar ⊙ gamma ⊙ B with the erase-gate output shape (B, T, H, d_k) (Equation 71).

Code has been implemented so that d(gamma) receives contributions from every site where gamma appears in the forward: E_bar rows, Q_gamma rows, K_tail rows via gamma_C/gamma_r, and the state normalization S = Diag(gamma) · S_hat (Equation 80).

Code has been implemented so that dg is obtained from d(gamma) using gamma = exp(G) and G_r = sum_{i<=r} g_i, via elementwise dG = gamma ⊙ d(gamma) followed by a reverse cumulative sum along the sequence axis (Equation 82).
L2 normalization and short-conv backward: route dQ and dK from the recurrence-side gradients back through per-head L2 normalization to the pre-normalization q, k.

Code has been implemented so that gradients dQ_normalized and dK_normalized (produced by the chunk backward) are passed through the standard per-head L2-normalization vector-Jacobian product to yield dQ_pre and dK_pre.
Numerical correctness verification of the gate-aware backward against a tokenwise recurrent reference through autograd.
A gradient-check test exists that compares dQ, dK, dV, dB, dW, dg, and dS_0 from the chunkwise fused backward against autograd through the tokenwise Gated Delta Rule-2 recurrence (Eq. 29) in fp64.

In the fp64 reference gradient check, gradients w.r.t. Q, K, V, B, W, the log-decay g, and the initial state S_0 agree with the tokenwise autograd reference to machine precision (as claimed in Appendix D.6).
The gradient-check test sweeps multiple sequence lengths, head counts, key/value dimensions, chunk boundaries, packed variable-length layouts, and nonzero initial states, all of which pass.
In fp32 the backward gradients agree with the tokenwise reference at the expected tensor-core accumulation noise level, and in bfloat16 the error follows the bfloat16 mantissa (Appendix D.6).
Tied-gate backward reduction: verify that when b_r = beta_r · 1 and w_r = beta_r · 1, the Gated DeltaNet-2 backward reduces to the KDA scalar-beta backward.

Code has been implemented for a thin wrapper that sets b_r = beta_r · 1_{d_k} and w_r = beta_r · 1_{d_v}, and a test confirms that d(beta_r) computed via chain rule from dB and dW matches the KDA scalar formula (Equation 48).
Kernel dispatch and precision constraints for the fused backward.

On Hopper GPUs, the fused gate-aware WY backward kernel's Triton autotune search is restricted to two and four warps for the 64×64 accumulator to avoid the WGMMA layout assertion, while Ampere retains the full search space (Appendix C.4).

The backward kernels store the recurrent state and matrix-multiplication accumulators in fp32 and expose an explicit precision flag for the (I+T) triangular solve used to construct A (Appendix D.3, D.4).
The backward correctly handles packed variable-length batches by resetting gradient accumulation at sequence boundaries using cumulative sequence lengths, matching the forward layout (Appendix C.6).
Assemble the Gated DeltaNet-2 token mixer block and construct both recurrent-only and hybrid (with sliding-window attention) 1.3B architectures.
The Gated DeltaNet-2 token mixer block is implemented with all input projections, convolutions, normalizations, gate branches, and the recurrent operator wired together as in Figure 1.
Code has been implemented for the Q/K/V input paths, each consisting of a linear projection followed by a short causal convolution and a SiLU activation.
Code has been implemented so that L2 normalization is applied per-head to the query and key tensors after the SiLU on the Q/K paths, while the V path does not receive L2 normalization.

Code has been implemented for a separate log-decay branch that produces alpha_t via the Gated DeltaNet parameterization g_t = -softplus(a) * sigmoid(linear(x)) + delta, computed in fp32 before entering the recurrent kernel.

Code has been implemented for the channel-wise erase gate branch b_t = sigmoid(Linear_b(x)) with output shape (B, T, H, d_k), and for the channel-wise write gate branch w_t = sigmoid(Linear_w(x)) with output shape (B, T, H_v, d_v).

Code has been implemented for the output path: the recurrent output S_t^T q_t is RMSNormed, multiplied elementwise by a separate SiLU output gate produced from the block input, and then passed through a final linear output projection.

The block correctly supports grouped value heads: when H_v > H, the q, k, log-decay g, and b tensors are repeated across the value-head group axis before the recurrent operator, while v and w already live on the value-head axis.
Code has been implemented so that when the negative-eigenvalue variant is enabled, only the erase gate is scaled to lie in [0, 2]^{d_k} (via 2*sigmoid), while the write gate remains in [0, 1]^{d_v}.
The block correctly names and uses the log-decay tensor g distinct from the SiLU output gate; g refers only to the log-decay used in the recurrence, not to the output gate.
The recurrent-only 1.3B Gated DeltaNet-2 architecture is assembled by stacking Gated DeltaNet-2 token mixers and MLPs under the standard pre-norm residual block.
Code has been implemented for a recurrent-only model that alternates (Gated DeltaNet-2 mixer, MLP) blocks with residual connections and pre-normalization, with no attention layers.
The 1.3B recurrent-only configuration uses d_model = 2048, H = 16 heads with d_k = 128 and d_v = 128, yielding a per-layer recurrent state of H * d_k * d_v = 262,144 floats per batch element.

The total parameter count of the recurrent-only Gated DeltaNet-2 model matches 1.3B parameters within a small tolerance, consistent with matched-parameter comparisons against Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet, KDA, and Mamba-3.
The hybrid Gated DeltaNet-2 architecture is assembled by interleaving Gated DeltaNet-2 mixers with sliding-window attention layers as depicted in Figure 1 (left).

Code has been implemented for a repeated hybrid cell that contains, in order, a Gated DeltaNet-2 token mixer, an MLP, a sliding-window attention layer (SWA), and another MLP, each with residual connections and pre-normalization.
Code has been implemented for a sliding-window causal attention layer with a configurable fixed window size; at 1.3B hybrid training the window is set to 2K tokens.

The hybrid model preserves linear sequence scaling and a bounded attention cache: memory used by SWA does not grow beyond the fixed window, and the recurrent mixer contributes only fixed-size state per layer.

The total parameter count of the hybrid Gated DeltaNet-2 model matches 1.3B parameters within a small tolerance under the same head/dimension configuration as the recurrent-only variant plus SWA layers.
Weight initialization and normalization choices for the block follow the paper's recipe so that early recurrent-state magnitudes stay controlled.
All linear layers in the Gated DeltaNet-2 block are initialized with Xavier uniform weights using gain 2^{-2.5}, and biases (where present) are initialized to zero.
The block uses RMSNorm on the recurrent output prior to the SiLU output gate and final projection, matching the description of the block design.

The block behaves correctly end-to-end: given tokenized inputs it produces outputs of the expected shape and passes forward/backward without shape or dtype errors, and its reductions match the parent recurrences.

The Gated DeltaNet-2 block, given an input tensor of shape (B, T, d_model), returns an output tensor of the same shape (B, T, d_model) and supports gradient computation through all parameters, including the erase and write gate projections.

When the block's erase gate b_t is forced to equal beta_t * 1_{d_k} and w_t to equal beta_t * 1_{d_v} (tied-scalar configuration), the block's outputs numerically match a KDA reference implementation on random inputs to within tensor-core accumulation tolerance.

Numerical verification of the chunkwise algorithm against a tokenwise recurrent reference and verification that Gated DeltaNet-2 reduces to KDA and Gated DeltaNet under the appropriate gate-tying conditions.
Provide a tokenwise recurrent reference implementation of Gated Delta Rule-2 usable as ground truth for verification.

Code has been implemented for a tokenwise recurrent reference that computes S_t = (I - k_t e_t^T) D_t S_{t-1} + k_t z_t^T with e_t = b_t ⊙ k_t and z_t = w_t ⊙ v_t following Eq. 10, and returns outputs o_t = S_t^T q_t for all tokens.
Code has been implemented so the tokenwise reference supports fp64 precision for the state and accumulators to enable machine-precision correctness testing described in Section D.6.
Forward-pass correctness of the chunkwise algorithm relative to the tokenwise reference across configurations.

Code has been implemented for a test harness that sweeps random configurations covering different sequence lengths, head counts, key dimensions d_k, value dimensions d_v, initial states, packed variable-length layouts, and dtypes (fp64/fp32/bf16), as described in Section D.6.
The fp64 forward test asserts that chunkwise outputs and end-of-chunk states match the tokenwise recurrent reference to machine precision (absolute/relative error at the fp64 round-off level).

The fp32 and bf16 forward tests assert that forward-output errors relative to the tokenwise reference are within tensor-core accumulation noise (fp32) and bf16 mantissa precision, respectively, as described in Section D.6.
Backward-pass correctness of the chunkwise algorithm relative to autograd through the tokenwise reference.
Code has been implemented to compare gradients from the chunkwise backward pass against autograd differentiation of the tokenwise reference for Q, K, V, B, W, log-decay g, and the initial state S_0.
In fp64 reference tests, gradients w.r.t. Q, K, V, B, W, the log-decay, and the initial state agree with autograd to machine precision, matching the claim in Section D.6.
In fp32 and bf16 backward tests, gradient discrepancies remain within tensor-core accumulation noise (fp32) and bf16 mantissa precision, consistent with Section D.6.
Verification that gate-tying reductions collapse Gated DeltaNet-2 exactly onto KDA and Gated DeltaNet as described in Section A.5.
Code has been implemented that instantiates the KDA tying by setting b_t = beta_t * 1_{d_k} and w_t = beta_t * 1_{d_v} in the Gated DeltaNet-2 layer while leaving channel-wise decay alpha_t intact.
A numerical test asserts that under KDA gate tying, Gated DeltaNet-2 outputs, end-of-chunk states, and gradients agree with a reference KDA implementation to fp64 machine precision.
Code has been implemented that additionally ties the decay to a scalar via alpha_t = alpha_t * 1_{d_k} together with the KDA gate tying, producing the Gated DeltaNet recurrence.
A numerical test asserts that under the combined KDA+scalar-decay tying, Gated DeltaNet-2 outputs and gradients agree with a reference Gated DeltaNet implementation to fp64 machine precision.
